key_insight: Decouple optimization into a trusted first-order direction and a cheap zeroth-order step search, so LLM fine-tuning can adapt step size without full line search overhead.
engineering_relevance: This offers a lightweight way to stabilize and accelerate large-model training when fixed learning rates are too conservative or too aggressive.
method: Use a first-order optimizer to pick the descent direction.
Evaluate the objective only at a few points along that direction.
Fit a local 1D model and choose a curvature-aware step within a bounded interval.
evidence_signal: Across multiple language-model and dataset settings, ZFO often improved optimization and final performance over fixed-step first-order baselines, with the best local model varying by objective.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the chosen direction and on reliable shared-sample finite-difference estimates, so noisy objectives or poor interval choices may reduce gains.
paper_title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
